title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 11
paragraphs: This happened as soon as the Persians came to Miletus. After this, the Ionians, gathered at Lade, held meetings, at which others no doubt also made speeches to them, but especially the Phocaean commander Dionysius, who said: “Seeing that our affairs, Ionians, are set upon the razor's edge—whether we are to be free or slaves, and slaves to be treated as runaways—now therefore, if you are willing to take on hardships, you will have labor for the time being, but you will be able to overcome the enemy and be free. If, however, you continue to be self-indulgent and without discipline, I have no hope that you will not pay the penalty to the king for your revolt. No, do as I say, hand yourselves over to me, and I promise—if the gods grant equal conditions—that either the enemy will not fight us at all, or that if they do fight they will be greatly discomfited.”
